newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China bank's '96 profit may not be hit by cash loss.
newsitem.headline: China bank's '96 profit may not be hit by cash loss.

text.p: China's big Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd may not revise down its 1996 earnings despite Beijing's plan to seize profits from illegal share trading, analysts said on Friday.
"The seizure won't affect its 1996 profits or dividend," Yan Yong, an analyst at China Securities Co, told the Hong Kong-based newsletter, the China Securities Bulletin.
"As far as I know, the bank's 1996 profits did not include any of the seized money."
Beijing authorities earlier announced they would confiscate gains of 90.34 million yuan ($10.88 million) from the bank's trading of its own shares between March 1996 and April this year.
"A profit revision is unlikely as the company did not mention share trading gains in its 1996 financial statement," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Authorities also sacked He Yun, chairman of the nation's only domestically listed bank, and barred him from the finance sector for five years.
The bank declined to comment.
"I can tell you nothing until the end of a forthcoming shareholders' meeting," a Shenzhen Development Bank spokesman said.
The bank posted net profit of 787 million yuan for 1996 against 435 million for 1995. It proposed a five-for-10 bonus share issue and a cash dividend of 0.2 yuan per share.
The bank originally planned to present the dividend proposal at a shareholders' meeting on May 26, but it has delayed the meeting becasue of the probe into its share trading.
Trading in the bank's A shares would be suspended for five sessions starting on Friday, a statement released by southern China's Shenzhen bourse said.
Brokers said the suspension of the heavily index-weighted stock helped the city's domestic currency A share market move into positive territory.
The A share index ended the day up 4.40 percent at 431.09 after sliding 5.67 percent in early trade.

Beijing also dismissed the head of the Shanghai branch of the state-run Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and the chiefs of three major brokerage firms for speculative stock trades. This also contributed to the market's early slump, analysts said.
The Shenzhen Development Bank had been considered one of the Shenzhen bourse blue chips. It led a bull-run on the A market early this year though it has since given up some of the gains.
The bank's stock closed at 30.87 yuan on Thursday, compared with its 1997 high of 49.
The bank's chairman was quoted in May as saying the bank aimed to have total assets of 40 billion yuan by the end of this year, up 30 percent from the end-1996 figure.
He said deposits would top 30 billion yuan by the end of this year while profits would also rise sharply. He did not give a precise profit forecast.
The bank, which evolved from the merger of six agricultural credit cooperatives in the late 1980s, had 1.03 billion outstanding shares at the end of last year.
